author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Japan’s wholesale prices rose 7.6% in August from a year earlier, keeping pipeline inflation elevated before the Bank of Japan’s policy meeting next week.

The increase in the corporate goods price index was slightly above the 7.4% rise economists had forecast in a Reuters poll. July’s gain was revised to 7.7%. On a month-to-month basis, producer prices slipped 0.2% after a revised 0.4% increase in July.
The yen-based import price index climbed 24.8% from a year earlier, slowing from a revised 29.3% increase in July but still signaling substantial pressure from imported goods and currency moves.

Markets had nearly fully priced a Bank of Japan rate increase to 1.25% from 1%, Reuters reported. A separate poll expected the central bank to reach 1.25% next week and 1.75% in the second quarter of 2027. Those expectations are market forecasts, not announced decisions. The BOJ raised its policy rate to a 31-year high of 1% in June and left it unchanged in July.
dek: Producer prices stayed above forecasts in August, reinforcing expectations that the central bank could raise its policy rate next week.
headline: Japan wholesale inflation holds at 7.6% before Bank of Japan meeting
